title: Add meaningful tests to untested code (mutation-graded)
user_outcome: The customer's pricing code now has tests that actually catch a wrong price. If someone quietly breaks the discount tiers, the rounding, the tax base or the proration, the test suite says so before it reaches a customer's invoice.

source_integrity.note: The job is to add tests, not to edit the code. Any byte change under pkg/ is an automatic FAIL.

test_invocation.fallback: If `tests/` does not exist, discovery runs from the directory root instead, so a layout technicality is never scored as a testing failure.

killable_mutations.breaks: A customer ordering exactly 25 units silently loses their 10% discount.
Half-cent amounts round the wrong way, so totals drift by a cent.
A capped promo code gives away more money than the cap allows.
The customer is taxed on the pre-discount amount and over-charged.
A tax-exempt customer is charged tax.
A line with zero units is priced instead of rejected.
A 150-unit order gets the 5% discount instead of 15%.
Proration rounds up, so a part-month customer is over-charged a cent.

neutral_mutations.why: `min_qty <= qty` is the same test written the other way round.

neutral_mutations.old: return Invoice(gross, net, promo, tax, discounted + tax)
neutral_mutations.new: return Invoice(gross, net, promo, tax, tax + discounted)

neutral_mutations.why: An explicit clamp is the same clamp `min()` performs.

guard_self_test.why: A mutation harness in this project once called two good tests vacuous because its search matched a doc comment quoting the call. Before any survived/killed verdict is believed, the guard must demonstrate it still rejects both traps.

must_raise_VacuousMutation.old: Divide two integers, rounding halves away from zero.
must_raise_VacuousMutation.new: Divide two integers, rounding halves toward zero.
must_raise_VacuousMutation.trap: Anchor matches a docstring. The compiled constants really do change, so a bytecode-only guard would wave this through.

must_raise_VacuousMutation.old: # Tier order matters here: the first tier whose minimum is met wins.
must_raise_VacuousMutation.new: # Tier order does not matter here.
must_raise_VacuousMutation.trap: Anchor matches a comment. The parser attributes no statement to the line and the compiled program is byte-identical.

pass_condition: All 8 killable mutations are detected (the added test suite fails on each), all 3 neutral mutations survive (the suite still passes), the suite passes on the unmutated code, at least 6 tests are collected, and no byte under pkg/ changed.
fail_condition: FAIL if any of the following is true: (a) any file under pkg/ differs by one byte from the fixture; (b) the test suite does not pass against the unmutated code; (c) fewer than 6 tests are collected, or zero tests are collected; (d) any of the 8 killable mutations leaves the suite passing -- the tests do not catch a wrong price; (e) any of the 3 neutral mutations makes the suite fail, which means the tests are asserting on incidentals rather than on behaviour; (f) the suite is not runnable by the documented command.
unproven_condition: UNPROVEN, never FAIL, if the guard raises VacuousMutation for any killable or neutral mutation, or if either guard self-test trap fails to raise. A mutation that cannot be proven to have landed on executable code grades nothing, and must never be reported as a miss by the tests.
